title: A Macrophage Reporter Cell Assay to Examine Toll-Like Receptor-Mediated NF-kB/AP-1 Signaling on Adsorbed Protein Layers on Polymeric Surfaces
protocol: Prepare fibroblast media by combining 450 mL of DMEM, 50 mL of FBS, and 5 mL of penicillin/streptomycin.
Store the prepared fibroblast media at 4 °C for up to 3 months.
Prepare reporter macrophage growth media in 50 mL aliquots by combining 45 mL of DMEM, 5 mL of FBS, 5 μg/mL mycoplasma elimination reagent, and 200 μg/mL phleomycin D1.
Store the prepared reporter macrophage growth media at 4 °C for up to 3 months.
Prepare reporter macrophage assay media in 50 mL aliquots by combining 45 mL of DMEM, 5 mL of heat-inactivated FBS (HI-FBS), 5 μg/mL mycoplasma elimination reagent, and 200 μg/mL phleomycin D1.
Store the prepared reporter macrophage assay media at 4 °C for up to 3 months.
Dissolve poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) in chloroform at a concentration of 20 mg/mL using a 20 mL glass scintillation vial and magnetic stir bar.
Stir the solution for at least 2 hours until all solids are dissolved.
Pipette 400 μL of PMMA solution onto the center of a borosilicate glass microscope slide in a spin coater.
Spin the coated slides at 3000 rpm for 2 minutes.
Store prepared slides in a clean box sprayed and wiped with 70% ethanol for future use.
Measure water contact angle at two random positions on the surface of extra coated slides using a goniometer.
Attach 8-chamber sticky wells to PMMA coated-slides in a biological safety cabinet (BSC) using sterile forceps and following aseptic technique.
Press firmly on the top of the sticky wells to ensure strong attachment.
Incubate the slides with attached sticky-wells at 37 °C overnight to secure the seal.
Add 200 µL of cell culture grade water to each well to test the seal of the sticky wells.
Incubate at room temperature (RT) for 60 min and ensure no leakage before proceeding.
Aspirate the water, being careful not to disturb the PMMA coating.
Perform endotoxin-free water washes by adding 300 µL of endotoxin-free water to each well and incubating for 1 h (three times), 12 h, and 24 h prior to use.
Test endotoxin concentration of the slides to be used for cell culture.
Incubate 200 µL of endotoxin-free reagent water in one well of each slide for 1 hour.
Measure endotoxin concentration in the extract using an endpoint chromogenic endotoxin assay.
Bring all test samples (i.e., extracts) and endotoxin assay reagents to room temperature.
Reconstitute chromogenic reagent in assay buffer.
Allow the chromogenic reagent to dissolve for 5 minutes.
Gently swirl the dissolved reagent before use.
Cover all bottles with paraffin film when not in use.
Create a 5−8 point standard dilution curve of endotoxin ranging from the lower to the upper limit of the assay by performing serial dilutions in reagent water.
Prepare a positive control by diluting a known amount of endotoxin in unused test sample solution.
Dilute the concentration of the positive control to match a standard in the middle of the standard curve.
Add 50 μL of standards, samples, or spike controls to each well of a 96-well plate in duplicate or triplicate.
Use reagent water as a negative control.
Add 50 µL of chromogenic reagent to every well quickly.
Cover the plate with an adhesive seal and incubate at 37 °C for the time specified on the Certificate of Analysis included in the chromogenic reagent kit.
Add 25 µL of 50% acetic acid to each well (final concentration of 10% acetic acid per well).
Read absorbance of the plate using a plate reader at 405 nm.
Ultraviolet (UV) sterilize the slides for 30 min prior to cell culture experiments.
Mix polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) elastomer in a 10:1 weight ratio (base:curing agent).
Pipette approximately 10 mL of polydimethylsiloxane base into a sterile tube.
Weigh the tube and slowly add curing agent until 10% has been added.
Thoroughly mix the elastomer by stirring with a sterile serological pipette tip and by pipetting up and down.
Add approximately 200 μL of the solution to each well of a 48-well plate.
Tilt the well plate slowly to ensure complete coverage of wells with elastomer solution.
Place the well plate with elastomer into a vacuum oven set at 50 cmHg, 40 °C.
Remove the lid and cover with a single-ply wipe to prevent other debris from falling into the wells.
Allow to incubate for at least 48 h.
Confirm the wells are completely coated via visual inspection.
Gently prod the elastomer with a sterile pipette tip to ensure it is fully cured before removing.
Add 300 µL of 70% ethanol (made with absolute ethanol and endotoxin-free water) and incubate at RT for 1 h.
Remove the ethanol and wash each well three times with 300 µL of endotoxin-free water, incubating for 1 h between each wash.
Incubate each well with 300 µL of endotoxin-free water for 12 h and then again for 24 h prior to use.
Incubate 200 µL of endotoxin-free water in three wells of each plate for 1 h.
Measure the endotoxin concentration of the water extracts using an endpoint chromogenic endotoxin assay (steps 2.5.1−2.5.6).
Make a 1 mg/mL solution of fluorinated poly(tetrafluoroethylene) by adding 10 mg of fPTFE to 10 mL of fluorinated solvent.
Stir the vial for at least 24 h until all solids are dissolved.
Add approximately 150 µL of the polymer solution to each well of a polystyrene 48-well plate.
Tilt the well plate slowly to ensure complete coverage of all wells with polymer solution.
Coat glass coverslips with fPTFE.
Place coated coverslips inside wells of a 24-well plate.
Add approximately 400 μL of polymer solution to each well containing a coverslip.
Push the coverslips down using sterile forceps to ensure complete coverage.
Cover the well plate with a lid.
Place the well plate into a vacuum oven set at 50 cmHg and 40 °C.
Remove the lid and cover the well plate with a single-ply wipe.
Incubate for at least 48 hours.
Measure water contact angle of fPTFE-coated coverslips using a goniometer.
Add 300 µL of 70% ethanol to each well and incubate at room temperature for 1 hour.
Remove the ethanol from the wells.
Perform endotoxin-free water washes by adding 300 μL of endotoxin-free water to each well and incubating for 1 hour (three times), 12 hours, and 24 hours prior to use.
Incubate 200 µL of endotoxin-free water in three wells of each plate for 1 hour.
Measure endotoxin concentration of water extracts using an endpoint chromogenic endotoxin assay.
UV sterilize the well plates for 30 minutes prior to cell culture experiments.
Grow 3T3 cells in multiple T150 flasks to 70% confluence.
Aspirate the media from the flasks.
Wash the surface with 5 mL of PBS and aspirate the PBS.
Add 5 mL of animal origin-free, recombinant cell dissociation enzyme.
Incubate at 37 °C for 3−5 min.
Gently tilt the flask back and forth to detach cells.
Add 5 mL of PBS to neutralize the recombinant enzyme used for cell dissociation.
Transfer detached cells from the flasks into a centrifuge tube.
Mix the cells via pipetting.
Perform a live cell count using a hemocytometer and cell viability dye.
Centrifuge the cells at 200 x g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in the original volume of PBS to wash off any remaining media.
Repeat the washing step.
Centrifuge the cells at 200 x g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Add PBS to achieve a final cell concentration of 1 x 106 cells/mL.
Place the cell solution into a -80 °C freezer until fully frozen (at least 2 h).
Thaw the cell solution in a 37 °C water bath.
Place the thawed solution back into the -80 °C freezer until totally frozen.
Repeat the freezing and thawing for a total of 3 freeze-thaw cycles.
Perform a micro bicinchoninic acid (BCA) assay on the cell lysate at various dilutions.
Dilute the cell lysate to a protein concentration of 468.75 µg/mL.
Aliquot the diluted cell lysate and store at -80 °C for future use.
Load 40−60 µg of lysate protein in loading buffer onto a 1.5 mm thick 10% polyacrylamide gel.
Follow standard Western blot procedures to assess presence of DAMPs (e.g., heat shock protein 60 [HSP60], high mobility group box 1 [HMGB1]).
Grow reporter macrophages in an appropriately sized flask to achieve 70% confluence.
Aspirate the media from the flask.
Wash the surface with PBS and then aspirate the PBS.
Add recombinant cell dissociation enzyme to the flask.
Incubate at 37 °C for 8 min.
Firmly tap the sides of the flask to detach cells.
Inactivate the enzyme by adding an equal volume of growth media (10% FBS).
Perform a live cell count using a hemocytometer and cell viability dye.
Centrifuge cells at 200 x g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in the original volume of PBS to wash them.
Centrifuge again.
Resuspend cells at 7.3 x 10^5 cells/mL in assay media (containing heat-inactivated FBS).
Separate the cell suspension into three different tubes: TLR4 inhibitor, anti-TLR2, and untreated.
Incubate cells with 1 µg/mL TLR4 inhibitor for 60 min at room temperature or with 50 µg/mL anti-TLR2 for 30 min at room temperature.

Add 200 µL of lysate, 10% FBS, 10% commercial mouse plasma, or a mixture of the protein solutions to a 48-well plate and allow the protein to adsorb at 37 °C for the desired time (i.e., 30 min, 60 min, or 24 h).
Aspirate the protein solution from the wells using a fresh Pasteur pipette for each protein solution.
Wash the surfaces with 250 µL of PBS for 5 min.
Aspirate the PBS.
Repeat washing and aspirating steps for a total of three washes.
Incubate cells at 37 °C for 20 h after adding TLR4 inhibitor or anti-TLR2 and resuspending the cells.
Sample 20 μL of supernatant from each well and plate in duplicate into a 96-well plate.
Add 200 µL of SEAP reporter assay reagent to each well.
Cover the plate with an adhesive seal and incubate for 2.5 h at 37 °C.
Transfer the remainder of the supernatant to a 1.5 mL tube (per well).
Centrifuge at 1,000 x g for 10 min to pellet any debris.
Transfer supernatant to a new 1.5 mL tube and store at -80 °C.
Analyze supernatant for the presence of proinflammatory cytokines via enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA).
Read absorbance of the plate using a plate reader at 635 nm.
